status.en: 6 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 60% fewer than the week before, most of them in Juba, Abiemnom and Warrap.
status.nb: 6 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 60 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Juba, Abiemnom og Warrap.

summary.en: Armed groups continue ambushing civilians, with killings reported in Jebel Boma County and a road ambush in Warrap County, while the SSPDF killed two Kapoeta youth after an arrest and the Kapoeta South Commissioner confirmed the killing of an SPLM secretary and a friend. A Christian woman was killed for refusing a forced marriage to a Muslim man and two pastors were wounded in a separate attack, prompting women in Greater Mundri to demand protection. The Ministry of Gender and stakeholders reviewed draft guidelines for safe houses for GBV survivors, and South Sudan condemned Iran missile and drone attacks in the Middle East. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Væpnede grupper fortsetter å overfalle sivile, med drap rapportert i Jebel Boma fylke og et veiambush i Warrap fylke, mens SSPDF drepte to unge fra Kapoeta etter en arrestasjon og Kapoeta sør-kommissær bekreftet drapet på en SPLM-sekretær og en venn. En kristen kvinne ble drept for å ha nektet et tvangsægteskap med en muslimsk mann, og to pastorer ble såret i et separat angrep, noe som fikk kvinner i Greater Mundri til å kreve beskyttelse. Kjønns- og likestillingsdepartementet og berørte aktører gjennomgikk utkast til retningslinjer for trygge hus for overlevende av kjønnsbasert vold, og Sør-Sudan fordømte Irans missil‑ og droneram i Midtøsten. To dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
